comment: You can expect quizzes often and a lot of reading, but professor Lefkowitz is very respectful and one of the best professors I've had.

Least favorite PPEl class I have taken which is disappointing for a senior seminar. The readings were dense and uninteresting and discussions in class were minimal. There was no real interaction with the material despite the topic itself being interesting. I think he is really nice and so smart but I got nothing out of the class.
Very knowledgeable on the topics so class was somewhat engaging. Little to no discussion time even when participation is graded. Readings were dense and exams were pretty demanding.

Was scared he was tough grader, but loved his class and he was very reasonable. Expectations super clear. Humor is so dry, but if you get it, he's hilarious. Incredibly smart, great in office hours, and lectures/slides SO CLEAR. Would definitely recommend, especially for philosophy majors. You'll learn a lot and you won't be bored.

Dr. Lefkowitz's class is amazing for anyone interested in criminal law! Although there is quite a bit of reading, I found that the subjects covered were extremely thought provoking. I think as long as you take advantage of office hours to discuss ideas for your papers before writing them, you will get a good grade. He is a fair grader.
A lot of reviews saying he's too hard. Only 4 papers in the semester which isn't too bad. The class was super interesting if you like ethics or philosophy. Would recommend

Dr. Lefkowitz is a great guy and knows his subject well. However, the class itself is difficult and requires a ton of writing. Hes also a very tough (but fair) grader. The class is open-ended and you get to focus on a topic of your choosing for the final paper, which is nice.

Dr. Lefkowitz has very high expectations for freshmen. He assigns very dense readings, a lot of homework and his feedback on papers is rather unclear. I wouldn't recommend his class, especially is this is your first time taking Philosophy.

Lefkowitz is really hard on students for his FYS class and not recommended if it is your first Philosophy class. Much of what he teaches requires more time than just a semester to learn and understand.

Lefkowitz is unnecessarily hard for an FYS class. He gives too much reading and expects too much from students. He is not a good professor especially if he is your first introduction to philosophy. His class is confusing, moves very fast and his feedback on essays and other work is rarely helpful. Would NOT recommend.

Dr. Lefkowitz is great. The readings are dense but as long as you go to class and take extensive notes the class is fine. Phil. of Law had 3 papers, and he is very clear on what he expects from you in each paper. I practically rewrote my notes in paper form and got good grades.

At first, I wanted to drop the class because I thought he was a boring professor. However, he is actually one of the smartest and most enjoyable professor to have. The topic is really intriguing and he teaches the materials very well

I at first found the class to be a bit dry, but I loved it by the end of the semester. Lefkowitz really wants students to do well - he distributes a tip sheet on what hes looking for in papers plus holds extra office hours to help revise papers, and his assignments are very clear. Not everyone ends up with an A, but its definitely possible.

At the beginning of the semester I wasn't sure how I'd like Lefkowitz, but having taken his class I can say I truly enjoyed having him as a professor. He can't be any clearer in class and loves discussion. He's also a really nice and genuine guy that wants to see you do well. Grades are 90% based on papers.
